report.title: Session discovery, work claims and file leases: prior art across agent and non-agent systems
report.question_or_target: How do mcp_agent_mail, Goose, OpenHands multi-agent, git worktrees, editor lockfiles and distributed lock services each answer the three questions - who else is running, who owns this work item, who holds this file - and which combination is implementable with no always-on server?
report.answer: None of the six examined systems natively answers all three questions without a server. mcp_agent_mail answers presence and file TTL reservations but delegates work-item authority to Beads and requires its HTTP FastMCP server. Goose and OpenHands answer parent-local activity only. Git worktrees give durable workspace/branch isolation without process liveness or per-file leases. Emacs lockfiles answer who holds one file via .#filename plus PID+boot stale detection. Consul/etcd answer all three via session/lease keys but require an always-on control plane. A cooperative same-host Linux combination of git worktrees, Emacs-style PID+boot metadata, and flock with close-on-exec plus explicit child-close is implementable with no always-on server; a surviving inherited descriptor keeps flock held, so that protocol is required. Cross-host authority still needs a live coordination service.

no_server_implementation.scope: cooperative agents owned by the same OS account and sharing one local Git common directory
combination: Git worktree per claimed work item for workspace/index isolation
Emacs-style readable owner metadata (host, PID, boot ID)
Linux flock held on open descriptors with FD_CLOEXEC and explicit child-close
protocol: Open the stable record path with FD_CLOEXEC, acquire LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB, write metadata, hold the descriptor for the ownership interval.
Do not fork after acquire unless the child immediately closes the lock descriptor; prefer a dedicated non-forking holder.
Discover sessions by scanning records: EWOULDBLOCK means a live cooperative holder; successful exclusive acquisition means stale metadata.
Use one worktree/branch per work item, but never infer liveness from the worktree record alone.
On crash the kernel closes descriptors; a surviving inherited descriptor keeps the lock, which is why child-close is required.
no_server_implementation.fencing_and_identity: record boot_id plus /proc/<pid>/stat starttime; mutation authority is lock ownership, never metadata age or file presence
hard_limits: Advisory flock only; uncooperative writers can ignore it.
